title: February and March 2022 Storm and flood disaster recovery small business grant – Guidelines
summary: This page provides guidelines for small businesses seeking disaster recovery funding following the February and March 2022 storm and flood events.
who_can_apply: Must be a small business affected by the February and March 2022 storm and flood disaster.
Must be located within a Defined Disaster Area.
Must meet specific criteria regarding the nature of the claimed costs and the business's ownership/use of assets.
what_you_need: A list and photographic evidence of the direct storm and flood-related damage.
Evidence of Payment for all amounts claimed, especially once the $25,000 limit is reached.
Documentation proving the cost was not ordinarily incurred without the disaster.
Financial records, photos, video evidence, or a statutory declaration to prove the items were used predominantly for business activities.

external_links.text: LGAs declared in (AGRN 1012) in Defined Disaster Areas

faqs.q: What types of costs can I claim for my small business?
faqs.a: Claimable costs include expenses that would not ordinarily have been incurred without the disaster, costs exceeding the labor to clean the property, replacing essential lost or damaged stock, and repairing or replacing motor vehicles directly damaged by the event.

faqs.q: Do I need to provide evidence of payment for my claim?
faqs.a: Evidence of Payment is required for all amounts claimed, including previous claims, once the $25,000 limit has been reached. For amounts between $25,000 to $50,000, Evidence of Payment is required at the time of application.

faqs.q: What is the maximum amount of funding available?
faqs.a: Funding amounts vary based on the applicant's location and the amount claimed, with limits mentioned up to $50,000.
